headline: Free Basics faces rejection: the very low-income users it targets are its fiercest critics, and net-neutrality alarm plus trust deficit outweigh hopeful access.
say_do_gap: People say they support it less (33%) than they would actually adopt it (42%), but both numbers are falling and the gap is narrowing as scrutiny rises.
summary: Support collapses from 42% to 33% over three rounds as net-neutrality and trust themes harden; the lowest-income segments (<₹35k), who represent the 'next billion' target, register the strongest opposition (net -0.48 and -0.46) despite voicing 'hopeful access' rhetoric. TRAI's consultation amplifies activist framing, turning a connectivity offer into a sovereignty threat.

drivers.explanation: 22% of discourse is 'Net Neutrality Alarm' — critics frame Free Basics as Facebook choosing India's internet; North region (n=85) net -0.22 reflects activist density.
11% 'Trust Deficit' theme; low-income users quote hidden costs and bait-and-switch: 'Facebook ko deta bhi milta hai' (construction worker, <₹15k).
Target segments <₹15k (net -0.48, adopt 29%) and ₹15–35k (net -0.46, adopt 39%) oppose most; high-income >₹2L (net +0.78, adopt 67%) support but don't need it.
18–24 segment only positive age group (net +0.24, adopt 50%); students see utility but flip negative when neutrality explained.

segments_at_risk.why: Most intended beneficiaries; net -0.48, adopt 29%; fear hidden recharges and limited utility beyond WhatsApp.
Large urban working class (n=85); net -0.46, adopt 39%; already pay ₹100+ for full data, see Free Basics as downgrade.
Net -0.65, adopt 24%; digitally cautious, distrust corporate motives, influenced by family warnings.

surprise: The 'Hopeful Access' theme (38% of discourse) is voiced by lower-income users, yet those same income segments show the most negative net sentiment — revealing a say/do split where gratitude for free access is overridden by suspicion of Facebook's gatekeeping.
fix: Replace Facebook-curated walled garden with a daily data-cap (e.g., 50 MB/day) usable on any site/app, administered by TRAI not Facebook, preserving net neutrality while keeping zero-rating economics.
rewrite: Reliance Communications, with TRAI oversight, launches 'Free Basics': a daily 50 MB zero-rated data allowance on any website or app the user chooses — no Facebook curation, no partner gatekeeping. Unused data rolls over. Funded by universal service obligation levy, not platform subsidies. Goal: connect the next billion Indians on their terms.
watch_outs: TRAI's February 2016 differential-pricing ruling will likely ban the current model; prepare compliance pivot now.
Reliance's retail reach could still distribute a neutral data-cap product if terms change.
WhatsApp-only utility perception caps adoption; any rewrite must visibly include banking, govt, education sites in demos.

backtest.actual_text: There was a large public backlash led by the #SaveTheInternet net-neutrality campaign. On 8 Feb 2016, TRAI banned discriminatory pricing for data services and Free Basics was shut down in India.
